newsitem.title: USA: Santander pleased with First Union outlook.
newsitem.headline: Santander pleased with First Union outlook.

text.p: Banco Santander SA is happy with the performance of First Union Corp and does not plan any further reductions in its First Union stake, Banco Santander Managing Director Jaime de Pinies said on Thursday.
"We do consider First Union's performance and outlook to be highly favorable," de Pinies said in a telephone interview. De Pinies was in New York today.
Earlier today Banco Santander said in a news release issued from Madrid that it had sold 2.1 million First Union shares in a block transaction on the New York Stock Exchange.

De Pinies said the reason for the sale of the 2.1 million shares -- and a sale of 3.6 million First Union shares on August 7 -- was that guidelines of the Bank for International Settlements require that stakes above 10 percent in non-consolidated companies be deducted from total capital.
According to the bank's press release, the August 7 stock sale reduced the stake below 10 percent, but then a decrease in First Union shares outstanding resulted in the ratio rising above 10 percent.
De Pinies said the stake was now "slightly above" nine percent and Santander would maintain it at more than nine percent.
